objectives.text: Given an alternating current (AC) waveform, DESCRIBE the relationship between average and RMS values of voltage and current, and the angular velocity within that waveform.

enabling.text: DESCRIBE the construction and operation of a simple AC generator.
EXPLAIN the development of a sine-wave output in an AC generator.
DEFINE the following terms in relation to AC generation:
DEFINE effective value of an AC current relative to DC current.
Given a maximum value, CALCULATE the effective (RMS) and average values of AC voltage.
Given a diagram of two sine waves, DESCRIBE the phase relationship between the two waves.

passages.quote: The elementary AC generator (Figure 1) consists of a conductor, or loop of wire in a magnetic field that is produced by an electromagnet.
The two ends of the loop are connected to slip rings, and they are in contact with two brushes.
the coil sides are moving parallel to the field and do not cut magnetic lines of force.
The horizontal coil is moving perpendicular to the field and is cutting the greatest number of magnetic lines of force.
rotation of the coil through 360° results in an AC sine wave output.
The time it takes for the generator to complete one cycle is called the period, and the number of cycles per second is called the frequency (measured in hertz).
Effective value of AC is the amount of AC that produces the same heating effect as an equal amount of DC.
The values of current (I) and voltage (E) that are normally encountered are assumed to be RMS values
Phase angle is the fraction of a cycle, in degrees, that has gone by since a voltage or current has passed through a given value.
The voltage e1 is said to lead e2 by 60 electrical degrees, or it can be said that e2 lags e1 by 60 electrical degrees.
If the phase difference between two currents, two voltages, or a voltage and a current is zero degrees, they are said to be "in-phase."
One cycle of the sine wave is generated when the coil rotates 2π radians.

body.alt: A loop of wire rotating between the poles of an electromagnet, with its ends on two slip rings and two brushes connected to a load.

body.text: When the loop rotates it cuts magnetic lines of force, first in one direction and then the other.
In the vertical position, there is no voltage induced in the loop:
Voltage and current increase to a maximum when the coil is horizontal to the magnetic lines of force, at 90°.
As the coil continues to turn, voltage and current decrease to zero at 180°. In the other half revolution, an equal voltage is produced with the polarity reversed.

body.alt: Sine wave of voltage against degrees of rotation, with a drawing of the loop position at 0, 90, 180, 270, and 360 degrees.

checks.q: In an elementary AC generator, what are the two ends of the loop connected to?
checks.x: The two ends of the loop are connected to slip rings, and they are in contact with two brushes.

checks.q: At what coil position is the induced voltage at its maximum?
o: Vertical, moving parallel to the field
Horizontal, moving perpendicular to the field
checks.x: The horizontal coil is moving perpendicular to the field and is cutting the greatest number of magnetic lines of force.

body.text: As the generator coil rotates 360°, the output voltage goes through one complete cycle.

body.alt: A rotating loop beside one cycle of a sine wave, with numbered points marking the phase around the cycle.

body.text: Angular velocity is expressed in radians per second, and 2π radians is a full revolution. One radian equals 57.3 degrees.

checks.q: What is the period of an AC wave?
o: The number of cycles per second
The time to complete one cycle
checks.x: The time it takes for the generator to complete one cycle is called the period.
The number of cycles per second is called the frequency, measured in hertz.

body.text: The peak value is the maximum voltage or current for an AC sine wave. The peak-to-peak value is the range spanned by the sine wave.
The value most commonly used for AC is the effective value.
One ampere effective value of AC produces the same amount of heat in a conductor, in a given time, as one ampere of DC.
The effective value is the root of the mean square of the currents, so it is known as the RMS value.

body.alt: A current sine wave above a curve of current squared, with the effective value and average value marked.

body.text: Other conversions: peak = average x 1.57, RMS = average x 1.11, peak = RMS x 1.414, and average = RMS x 0.9.

checks.q: Effective value of AC is the amount of AC that produces the same what as an equal amount of DC?
checks.x: Effective value of AC is the amount of AC that produces the same heating effect as an equal amount of DC.

checks.q: The peak voltage of an AC wave is 100 volts. What is the RMS value?
checks.x: Effective value (RMS) = peak value x 0.707 = 70.7 volts.

checks.q: The peak voltage of an AC wave is 100 volts. What is the average value?
checks.x: Average value = peak value x 0.637 = 63.7 volts.

body.text: The given value is normally zero. Phase difference describes two voltages of the same frequency that pass through zero in the same direction at different times.

body.alt: Two sine waves, e1 and e2, with the same frequency plotted against electrical degrees. e1 crosses zero 60 degrees ahead of e2.

body.text: If the phase difference is an amount other than zero, they are out-of-phase.

checks.q: Wave A passes through zero 60 degrees before wave B. How is this described?
checks.x: The wave that passes through zero first leads. In the handbook's example, e1 leads e2 by 60 electrical degrees.

checks.q: Two voltages have a phase difference of zero degrees. How are they described?
checks.x: If the phase difference is zero degrees, they are said to be in-phase.

facts.q: What is the peak voltage of an AC sine wave?
facts.a: The maximum voltage for an AC sine wave. The value of Emax occurs at 90°.
The fraction of a cycle, in degrees, that has gone by since a voltage or current has passed through a given value.

facts.q: How much rotation generates one cycle of the sine wave?
facts.a: One cycle is generated when the coil rotates 2π radians.

facts.q: What kind of values are normally assumed for AC current and voltage?
Convert a peak value to an effective (RMS) value.

summary.text: A simple generator is a conductor loop turning in a magnetic field, cutting across the magnetic lines of force.
Each half turn of rotation produces one half of the cycle of AC generation.
Radians/second is the velocity the loop turns, hertz is the number of cycles in one second, and period is the time to complete one cycle.
I = 0.707 Imax is the effective current, and E = 0.707 Emax is the effective voltage.
Phase angle is used to compare two wave forms by degrees of rotation.
